newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: First SA Foods roars ahead at debut.
newsitem.headline: First SA Foods roars ahead at debut.

text.p: Debutante foods firm First South African Foods Ltd got off to a roaring start on its first day's trading, dealers said on Tuesday.
The firm, which had been offered at an issue price of 200 cents, surged to 375 cents as dealers poured into the stock.
By 0820 GMT more than 2.81 million shares changed hands in trade worth 10.06 million rand, making it the most heavily traded stock on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange early on Tuesday.
"There are a lot of guys chasing the shares today," one dealer said.

They said the share rise had been so marked because the public offer had been limited with the majority of shares being retained by holding firm First South Africa Holdings (FSAH), management or offered to institutions in a private placing.
"There was only a small public offering which was therefore massively oversubscribed. It has been a very successful listing," one dealer added.
The firm, which invests in niched food manufacturing operations, aims to use the cash raised in the flotation to pursue a number of expansion oppoertunites.
First Food owns four operating companies, namely Piemans Pantry, Astoria Bakery, Seemann's Quality Meat Products and Gull Food.
FSAH is a sibling of Nasdaq-quoted firm First South Africa Corp.
